summary: Build a raw balance with faders and panning before adding corrective processing.
rationale: A stable starting balance makes later EQ, compression, and effects decisions easier to evaluate.
safety_notes: Do not raise live faders above 0 dBFS without operator approval.

summary: Use EQ only to solve an identified tonal, masking, or translation problem.
rationale: Reasoned EQ avoids stacking habitual boosts and keeps changes explainable.
safety_notes: Prefer cuts for feedback-prone live channels unless the operator approves boosts.

summary: Use compression when level variation, envelope shape, or density needs control.
rationale: Compression should stabilize or shape a source, not be applied as a default decoration.
safety_notes: Do not use makeup gain to bypass headroom limits.

summary: When compression audibly lowers a source, restore only the lost level with bounded output or makeup gain.
rationale: Makeup gain should make the compressed signal comparable in level for evaluation, while preserving true-peak headroom and avoiding bleed or noise lift.
safety_notes: Do not use makeup gain to bypass headroom limits or pull bleed/noise forward.

summary: Check phase and polarity before making tonal decisions on multi-mic sources.
rationale: Comb filtering can masquerade as EQ problems, especially on drums and other multi-mic setups.
safety_notes: Phase checks are analysis-only until an operator or safe offline path applies them.

summary: Keep low-frequency foundation stable and avoid widening sub/low-bass content.
rationale: Low-end stereo problems can reduce translation and waste headroom.
safety_notes: Never widen sub-low content in live PA without measurement and operator approval.

summary: Use panning to clarify roles: keep critical anchors stable and move supporting sources aside.
rationale: Sound-field placement is a primary mix tool, not merely a decoration.
safety_notes: Keep live vocal intelligibility and mono compatibility ahead of width.

summary: Use reverb as depth, and filter returns so ambience does not cloud low end or presence.
rationale: Filtered shared ambience can create space while preserving front-image clarity.
safety_notes: Avoid adding low-frequency reverb to kick/bass unless explicitly desired.

summary: Use filtered delay or slap to add vocal dimension when reverb would blur articulation.
rationale: Delay can create depth and audibility while keeping the dry source forward.
safety_notes: Keep delay returns below feedback-prone vocal monitor paths in live use.

summary: Set supporting microphones by phase, contribution, and desired color rather than a fixed numeric ratio.
rationale: A bottom snare or room mic should support the main image without becoming an unverified rule.
safety_notes: Do not treat any exact support-mic offset as source-grounded unless the source states it.

summary: When a source sounds harsh, prefer a small targeted cut on the offending band before broad tonal changes.
rationale: Small corrective moves preserve the balance and avoid over-darkening the mix.
safety_notes: For live vocals, confirm the cut does not hide intelligibility.

summary: If the mix is muddy, identify the contributing source and use modest low-mid cleanup instead of global overcorrection.
rationale: Mud is often source-specific; broad master cuts can thin important instruments.
safety_notes: Avoid excessive low-mid cuts on single-source live channels without A/B check.

summary: Automatic mix decisions should be bounded, inspectable, and logged with the source rule that justified them.
rationale: Learning from automated mixing requires stable data representation and traceable evaluation.
safety_notes: Logging must not block real-time audio or OSC paths.

summary: Use loudness and true-peak measurements as technical safety descriptors, not as a substitute for musical judgment.
rationale: Meters help prevent overload and compare levels, but they do not decide the artistic balance alone.
safety_notes: Do not raise gain only because LUFS is below a target.

summary: Treat masking as a targeted problem: reduce the worst instrument/frequency outliers rather than trying to remove all spectral overlap.
rationale: Research on multitrack masking shows masking reduction can improve clarity, while AES work warns that some masking is normal or desirable and automatic systems should focus on problematic outliers.
safety_notes: Avoid broad automatic cuts that erase intentional blend or destabilize live monitor translation.

summary: Use stereo placement to reduce masking for supporting sources while keeping lead vocal, kick, snare, bass, and low-end anchors stable.
rationale: AES spatialization research frames panning as a masking-reduction tool, but practical panning still depends on role hierarchy and mono-compatible anchors.
safety_notes: Check mono compatibility and avoid widening sub-low content.

summary: For automatic level setup, use simple loudness/energy descriptors as a stable first balance, then correct by instrument role and masking context.
rationale: AES level-adjustment work reports that simple loudness features can be competitive for automatic level setting; standards describe measurement, not artistic balance.
safety_notes: Never raise live faders above 0 dBFS without explicit operator approval.

summary: Prefer automation or modest compression for level consistency before flattening sources with heavy fast compression.
rationale: Professional guidance emphasizes compression for clear needs, warns it can raise room/noise, and recommends automation for large vocal level discrepancies when transparency matters.
safety_notes: Do not use makeup gain to bypass headroom limits or pull bleed/noise forward.

summary: When drums need more weight, prefer a blended/parallel density path or conservative bus compression over crushing the main kit image.
rationale: SOS drum guidance describes parallel drum compression as a way to add low-level detail and body while preserving performance dynamics better than heavy insert compression.
safety_notes: Time-align any parallel path and watch cymbal/room pumping.

summary: Shape drum attack and body with compressor timing: preserve kick attack with slower attack when click is missing, and use faster timing only when body/density is the goal.
rationale: SOS rock/metal mixing guidance ties compressor attack/release choices directly to transient retention, body, and perceived aggression.
safety_notes: Confirm compressor timing does not overemphasize bleed or cymbal hash.

summary: Create vocal and backing depth with filtered sends, delay, and pre-delay rather than simply adding louder unfiltered reverb.
rationale: SOS depth guidance connects distance with level, tone, reverb amount, delay, and pre-delay; busy mixes often need less wash and more controlled ambience.
safety_notes: Keep low-frequency reverb away from kick and bass unless explicitly desired.

summary: Build low end with headroom first: protect master/channel peaks, give kick weight in the 40-80 Hz region, and avoid confusing loudness normalization with bass balance.
rationale: Official loudness standards define measurement and true peak safety, while producer guidance emphasizes gain staging and targeted kick/bass weight rather than clipping the master bus.
safety_notes: Do not boost low end if true peak or PA headroom is already constrained.

summary: When vocal needs edge, consider harmonic density or small presence shaping before large high-frequency boosts that exaggerate esses.
rationale: Producer guidance notes that adding edge only with high-end EQ can make sibilants and consonants harder to control; source-grounded moves should watch harshness metrics.
safety_notes: Do not brighten feedback-prone live vocals without checking harshness and sibilance.

summary: Keep automatic mixing outputs as conventional, inspectable console parameters instead of opaque end-to-end transformations.
rationale: Recent automatic mixing research favors differentiable or learned systems that still expose level, pan, EQ, dynamics, and effect controls for human adjustment and post-hoc correction.
safety_notes: Opaque learned decisions must not bypass live safety gates or operator review.

summary: For multi-miked drums, audition polarity and small delay candidates against a chosen reference, then keep only changes that improve punch, body, mono compatibility, and full-mix translation.
rationale: AES and SOS guidance frame phase/time alignment as an early diagnostic before EQ or compression, but warn that visually perfect alignment can damage bleed relationships, cymbals, room tone, or mono playback.
safety_notes: In live mode, keep delay changes shadow-first and bounded because channel delay can affect monitoring, feel, and bleed relationships.
Do not align every drum mic to every other mic; use role-specific references and reject candidates that improve solo tone while worsening the kit or mono mix.

summary: Use shared, fully wet FX returns with filtered low and high end, then set send/return levels in full mix context rather than in solo.
rationale: Professional reverb guidance treats send returns as shared spaces, warns that reverb can quickly create mud, and recommends pushing a return until it is audible then backing it down in the complete mix.
safety_notes: Keep kick, bass, and sub-low energy out of shared wet returns unless explicitly requested.
FX returns must not mask vocal intelligibility or consume true-peak headroom.

summary: Use pre-delay as a role-dependent clarity tool: longer for front sources needing separation, shorter on drums so transients stay punchy without flamming.
rationale: Manufacturer and SOS guidance describe pre-delay as a way to keep dry attacks clear before the reverb blooms, while warning that the exact value is a starting point to audition in context.
safety_notes: Treat ranges as audition starts, not fixed prescriptions; reject values that smear rhythm or push lead vocal behind the mix.

summary: In dense mixes, prefer filtered tempo delay or delay feeding reverb when long reverb would blur articulation or crowd the midrange.
rationale: SOS and FabFilter guidance note that delay can create a sense of space while taking less mix real estate than lush reverb, especially when repeats are tempo-synced, filtered, and allowed to recede.
safety_notes: Keep repeats below lead consonants; in live use, avoid feedback-prone vocal monitor paths and excessive feedback values.

summary: Ducking a reverb or delay return from the dry source can keep the front signal intelligible while allowing ambience to bloom in phrase gaps.
rationale: SOS and FabFilter guidance describe sidechain-ducked FX returns and controlled/gated ambience as ways to add depth without washing over vocals or drums.
safety_notes: Do not let ducking pump the whole mix; sidechain only the relevant FX return and keep the dry source stable.

summary: Use chorus, phaser, or flanger mainly as support-source width, depth, and texture on filtered sends/returns, keeping lead anchors clear and using flanger/phaser as more obvious color only when intended.
rationale: SOS, iZotope, and Eventide guidance describe chorus as a width/thickening tool, flanger as stronger comb-filter motion, and phaser as a more nuanced moving-notch effect; all can reduce presence if overused.
safety_notes: Avoid widening kick, bass, lead vocal, or snare anchors with modulation unless it is a deliberate special effect.
Check mono compatibility because modulation uses phase/time differences.

summary: Choose modulation placement intentionally: modulation before reverb textures the tail more subtly, while modulation after reverb makes the whole ambience move.
rationale: SOS reverb treatment guidance states that chorus or flanger before reverb is diffused into a textured space, but after reverb the full tail is modulated and becomes much more audible.
safety_notes: Moving reverb tails can distract from vocal timing; keep this shadow/advisory for live use unless the operator requests an obvious effect.

summary: Use early reflections, diffusion, and late-tail balance to place sources: early energy defines proximity and surfaces, while late tail and modulation create size and motion.
rationale: Lexicon and Valhalla documentation separates early reflections/pre-echoes from late reverberation and ties diffusion, crossfeed, spin, and wander to density, naturalness, and spatial imaging.
safety_notes: Do not chase large ambience at the expense of mono imaging, lyric intelligibility, or drum transient focus.

summary: Build the musical picture with level, pan, mute/edit, and source intent before leaning on EQ, compression, or master processing.
rationale: Core mixing texts and professional interviews repeatedly frame processing as support for a chosen balance, not a replacement for one.
safety_notes: In live mode, balance moves still obey fader ceiling, headroom, and feedback checks.

summary: Use level planes by musical role: anchors, foreground, support, ambience, and effects should have stable relative depth before fine tonal moves.
rationale: AYAIC-style level-plane balancing matches broader mix literature on arranging sources into foreground/background and avoids confusing absolute loudness with musical hierarchy.
safety_notes: Do not push anchors above safe headroom just to satisfy a level-plane target.

summary: Treat the mix as a three-dimensional sound stage: left-right width, front-back depth, and frequency/timbre placement must support the song role of each source.
rationale: Moylan and Gibson describe sound stage and perceived image as musical structure; panning, level, EQ, and ambience should work together rather than as isolated moves.
safety_notes: Stereo width cannot come at the expense of mono low-end stability or vocal intelligibility.

summary: Prefer transparent master-bus gain, headroom, and dynamics preservation over loudness chasing or heavy limiting.
rationale: Mastering and loudness literature warns that loudness maximization can damage musical quality; standards describe measurement, while listening and headroom decide whether processing is acceptable.
safety_notes: Do not increase loudness if it creates clipping, aggressive compression, or unstable tonal balance.

summary: Treat every mix decision as playback-dependent: verify translation with meters, mono, headphones/speakers when available, and avoid overfitting to one room or PA resonance.
rationale: Recording and reproduction sources emphasize that loudspeakers, room response, and monitoring level strongly affect tonal and spatial judgment.
safety_notes: In live PA, reduce risk and preserve headroom when room/PA response is uncertain.

summary: Use masking, loudness, sharpness, and timbre descriptors as context for targeted decisions, not as a command to remove all overlap or brightness.
rationale: Psychoacoustic models explain why some sources hide or fatigue others, but musical blend often requires controlled overlap and listener-context judgment.
safety_notes: Avoid broad automated tonal changes when the perceptual problem is not persistent across sections.

summary: Use objective metrics and MuQ-style evaluators as feedback layers, while final acceptance remains constrained by safety, engineering checks, and operator listening feedback.
rationale: IMP research and listening-test standards show that automatic systems need measurable feedback, but objective metrics are domain-limited and must be calibrated against human perception.
safety_notes: MuQ-A1 or any quality model must never directly bypass OSC safety/rate-limit layers.

summary: Represent automatic mix choices as conventional console parameters with before/after metrics, source IDs, and rollback data.
rationale: Knowledge-engineered and differentiable mixing research both become safer when the output is inspectable level, pan, EQ, dynamics, FX, or bus data rather than opaque audio-only edits.
safety_notes: Opaque learned transformations stay offline-only unless explicitly approved and wrapped by safety checks.

summary: In offline tests, never use hidden final mixes, dataset labels, or filenames as decision shortcuts; decisions must come from audio, safe rules, metrics, and declared references only.
rationale: Research datasets are valuable for training/evaluation, but honest automatic mixing experiments require preventing reference leakage and metric overfitting.
safety_notes: Dataset-derived decisions must not send live OSC commands.

summary: Choose effects by intended function: space, depth, width, motion, density, special color, or repair; preset names and famous chains are only starting vocabulary.
rationale: Effects history and mix texts show that time/modulation/nonlinear effects are creative tools whose value depends on context, not on copying a preset or named engineer chain.
safety_notes: In live mode, keep FX sends conservative and reversible unless the operator asks for an obvious effect.

summary: Use interviews and professional series for transferable engineering principles, but never imitate a named engineer, artist, or trademark sound as a target.
rationale: Professional corpora reveal general habits such as intent, arrangement awareness, automation, contrast, and A/B discipline, while exact style replication is neither reliable nor appropriate.
safety_notes: When the user asks for a famous-engineer direction, translate it into generic audio attributes and ask for/measure a reference instead of cloning identity.

summary: Before correcting a channel, decide whether it is an anchor, lead, support, texture, room, or playback element, then scale EQ, dynamics, pan, and FX by that role.
rationale: Mix books and professional case studies emphasize that a source's job in the arrangement determines whether it should be forward, tucked, dry, wet, wide, narrow, bright, or dark.
safety_notes: Role-based boosts still require headroom, feedback, and true-peak checks.

summary: Kick: body boost 55-80 Hz, box cut 250-500 Hz, beater attack 2.5-4 kHz, HPF 30-40 Hz.
rationale: Positive tonal goals for kick instead of only cutting protruding peaks: fundamental body anchors the mix, box cut removes woody knock, beater click keeps timing audible in a live mix.
safety_notes: Live boosts require true-peak headroom and no feedback-prone ring; prefer cuts when unsure.

summary: Snare: HPF ~100 Hz, body 200-400 Hz, smack 2-4 kHz, gentle air 6-10 kHz.
rationale: Snare needs body plus crack to read in a live mix; air is seasoning, not a goal.
safety_notes: Snare T/B pair is ONE instrument: tonal targets apply to the blend, bottom mic follows the stereo-identity replica.

summary: Toms: HPF ~40 Hz, careful thump 100-300 Hz, attack 3-5 kHz.
rationale: Tom close mics need attack definition; excess 100-300 Hz boost stacks mud across the kit.
safety_notes: Bleed-dominated tom mics get NO tonal EQ (bleed rule): gate only.

summary: Overheads: HPF 100-200 Hz, sparing 200-400 Hz clank cut, gentle 8-15 kHz air.
rationale: OH pair is the drum master image: keep it clean of low-mid clank and open on top without hyping.
safety_notes: OH L/R processed identically (stereo pair identity).

summary: Bass: HPF 25-40 Hz, body 80-200 Hz, mud cut 250-500 Hz, definition 700-1200 Hz.
rationale: Bass reads through body plus note definition; the 250-500 mud zone fights guitars and vocals.
safety_notes: Kick owns 50-80 Hz: bass body boost sits above the kick fundamental region.

summary: Electric guitar: HPF 80-120 Hz, watch 150-300 Hz body, modest presence 3-6 kHz.
rationale: Guitars translate through upper-mid presence; their low end mostly duplicates bass and kick energy.
safety_notes: L/R pair processed identically; masking cuts must not touch the vocal presence core deeper than -3 dB.

summary: Lead vocal: HPF ~100 Hz, mud cut 200-500 Hz, presence 2.5-4.5 kHz, gentle air 8-14 kHz.
rationale: Vocal presence 2.5-4.5 kHz is what separates buried from readable; air boosts are feedback bait live and stay small.
safety_notes: Presence/air boosts on a live vocal require feedback headroom; formants are the voice, not a problem to cut.

summary: Preamp/trim sets nominal level ONCE with headroom; the mix is made with faders, never by re-riding preamps.
rationale: Re-mixing with preamps destroys gain structure downstream (comp thresholds, gate points, sends all shift). Operator complaint 2026-07-06: kick trimmed down then pushed back up with fader.
safety_notes: Live trim boosts remain opt-in (bleed can look like a quiet source).

summary: Digital console nominal: ~-18 dBFS RMS with peaks around -12 dBFS — the headroom/SNR compromise.
rationale: EBU-derived convention: -18 dBFS = old 0 dBu/0 VU; keeps ~18 dB headroom for transients and EQ boosts while staying above the noise floor.
safety_notes: True peak < -1 dBTP before any gain raise (CLAUDE.md).

summary: Keep working faders in the high-resolution zone near unity; global level moves belong to DCA/groups, not deep channel fader parking.
rationale: Near the fader bottom one step is ~10 dB; near unity ~0.25 dB. A balance living at -40 has no usable resolution and drifts.
safety_notes: Mutes remain proposal-only; never lift a parked fader automatically.

summary: Dynamics on an L/R pair must be sidechain-linked: identical settings alone let the image wander when one side compresses harder.
rationale: A stereo-linked compressor reduces both channels by the same amount whenever either side triggers; independent detectors with equal settings still produce unequal GR on asymmetric material, shifting the stereo image on transients.
safety_notes: Engine currently replicates settings only (stereo identity pass); console link surface not yet automated.

summary: Mono-fold health: correlation near +1..0 is fine, below 0 means out-of-phase content; keep low end and lead vocal mono; hard-panned sides lose ~6 dB in mono.
rationale: Sub frequencies are non-directional and phase-prone; a negative L/R correlation signals cancellation that turns the mono fold hollow. Hard-panned sources exist on one channel only and drop ~6 dB when summed.
safety_notes: Operator scheme pans pairs hard L/R on a stereo PA by explicit directive; mono-fold loss accepted, monitored via master_mix_eval correlation/mono_fold_ratio.

summary: Polarity is a binary fix and comes FIRST: flip the suspect mic of a related pair; fatter = keep, thinner = flip back. Only then time-align.
rationale: A polarity error masquerades as a delay/EQ problem; resolving the binary decision first keeps time alignment honest. Fader-pull diagnostic: if the drum gets LOUDER when a mic is pulled down, that mic cancels.
safety_notes: Polarity from correlation sign only AFTER lag compensation (CLAUDE.md: r at zero lag fails on shifted wideband snare).

summary: Overheads are the drum time reference: choose once, never move; close mics are delayed INTO the OH picture (~1 ms per foot of distance difference).
rationale: OHs capture the kit as one coherent instrument; moving the reference mid-process invalidates every prior alignment. Expected close-to-OH deltas: snare ~2-4 ms for typical 3 ft overheads.
safety_notes: Matches operator scheme 2026-07-06 (OH-anchored order); proper alignment can add up to ~6 dB of coherent sum — use sum energy as trial metric.

summary: Do not over-align: room mics are never time-aligned, toms may keep small offsets for depth; if everything aligned sounds flatter — step back.
rationale: Small phase differences create spatial depth; perfectly aligning every mic flattens the kit into a triggered-sample sound. Verify by ear and in mono, not only by waveform.
safety_notes: Mono fold ratio from master_mix_eval is the stress test; a worse mono fold after alignment = rollback.

summary: Live compression per role: vocal 2:1-3:1 soft knee GR 2-4 dB (peaks 5-10); snare/kick 4:1-6:1 GR 2-4; bass 2:1-4:1 attack >=20 ms; drum bus 2:1 GR 1-2.
rationale: Cross-corroborated role table: gentle ratios keep vocals natural, drums take higher ratios with fast-but-not-instant attack, bass needs the transient through (attack under ~20 ms robs punch), bus compression is glue not control.
safety_notes: Makeup restores lost level (operator rule); GR ceiling 8 dB per safety config.

summary: A compressor must NOT work 100% of the time: it should breathe — engage on peaks, release between phrases; audible pumping or constant GR means misconfiguration.
rationale: Over-compression flattens the performance and draws attention to the processing; a healthy channel compressor idles part of the time. GR duty cycle is a measurable trial metric.
safety_notes: Complements comp_v3 PUMPING_LIMIT; degradation ladder already raises threshold when GR is useless.

summary: Low-end sources: release under ~50 ms distorts kick/bass tone (release rides individual waveform cycles); keep release above the source's period envelope.
rationale: On kick and bass, very fast release follows the waveform itself instead of the envelope, producing harmonic distortion and losing low-end weight.

summary: Lead vocal chain order: HPF 80-100 -> subtractive EQ (mud 200-400 cut 2-4, nasal 800-1k) -> compression (3:1-4:1, GR 2-4 avg / 6-10 peaks) -> de-ess 5-8k -> additive EQ (presence 3-5k, air 10k+) -> FX via sends.
rationale: Subtractive EQ before compression makes GR respond to the cleaned signal; additive boosts after compression survive intact; de-essing after compression catches the sibilance compression amplified.
safety_notes: WING: единый EQ-блок стоит ДО динамики в дефолтном порядке — прибавляющие бусты компрессируются; держать бусты скромными или менять порядок eq/dyn на канале.
Air-бусты на живом вокале — feedback-приманка, кэп +1.5-2 дБ.

summary: De-esser sits AFTER the compressor: compression raises sibilance; de-essing first lets the compressor bring esses right back.
rationale: GR on the loud body of a phrase lifts relative sibilance level; the de-esser must see the post-compression signal to catch it.
safety_notes: Де-эссер-поверхность WING в движке не автоматизирована; sibilance_excess детектор уже следит за полосой.

summary: Reverb/delay for vocals go on send/return buses only, never as channel inserts: independent wet/dry and no downstream processing of the tail.
rationale: An inserted reverb tail gets compressed and EQ'd with the voice, pumping and ducking unnaturally; a send keeps the tail clean and the dry vocal intact.
safety_notes: Совпадает с текущей архитектурой (FX-шины 13-15 с инсерт-гвардом).

summary: A quiet mix is fixed at the gain-staging stage (raise channel nominal toward -18 dBFS RMS / -12 peak at soundcheck), never by pushing the master or adding a bus limiter.
rationale: Pushing the master hides balance problems and destroys crest factor; level lives at the source nominal. Applies directly to the -29 LUFS case: stems below planes with cuts-only DCA means the SOURCES are under nominal.
safety_notes: Trim boost требует явного opt-in оператора (bleed-правило); буст только при подтверждённом собственном сигнале и true peak < -1 dBTP.

summary: Anchor mix loudness on drums at 9-12 dB FS headroom; balance everything else relative to the kit — the mix lands at healthy loudness with crest intact.
rationale: Drums are the crest-defining element; setting them first with 9-12 dB headroom and balancing the rest relatively keeps the sum inside loudness limits without bus processing.
safety_notes: Сосуществует с Ayaic-плоскостями: якорь задаёт абсолютный уровень, плоскости — относительный баланс.

summary: Live reverb: plate/room by default (halls only for ballads); vocal pre-delay 10-30 ms (up to 80 for separation); snare pre-delay ~40 ms, decay ~0.8 s.
rationale: Short pre-delay keeps the dry source transparent while the tail blooms behind it; halls smear fast material. Snare gets its own shorter space so it keeps impact.
safety_notes: Совпадает с текущим FX-рэком (PLATE/ROOM, слоты 1-8, инсерт-гвард).

summary: No reverb on kick, bass, cymbals/hi-hat: reverb muddles low-end clarity and turns cymbals splashy; drums get space via snare/tom sends only.
rationale: Low-frequency reverb energy is non-directional mud; cymbals already carry the room in overheads.
safety_notes: Дополняет close_mic_fx_sends_enabled=false.

summary: Delays are tempo-scaled (start ~250 ms, 2-3 repeats; shorter on fast songs); song room reverb decay tuned so a snare hit dies just before the next one; BGV doubling ~30 ms.
rationale: Effects that breathe with the tempo stay invisible; a snare tail crossing the next hit smears the groove. Outdoor stages need MORE reverb (no natural reflections).
safety_notes: Дилей-шина остаётся замьюченной до подтверждения темпа (текущая доктрина).

summary: Masking is resolved by cutting the NON-priority element: 2-3 dB wide-Q in the winner's core range (e.g. guitars/keys yield 2-4 kHz to the lead vocal); never boost the winner instead.
rationale: The mix has one owner per range; cutting competitors is transparent while boosting the winner shifts its timbre and eats headroom. Vocal priority is the default hierarchy.
safety_notes: Совпадает с erb_masking: срезы не глубже -3 в тембровом ядре маскера.

summary: Dynamic masking fixes: sidechain duck (kick->bass), multiband sidechain (guitars yield 800-5000 Hz only while the vocal is present), dynamic EQ for occasional overlaps.
rationale: A static cut costs the competitor its body all song long; a dynamic cut takes the range only when the priority element actually needs it and returns it after.
safety_notes: WING имеет выбор sidechain-источника у канальной динамики; поверхность в движке не автоматизирована — shadow до отдельной задачи.

summary: Masking detection: does the key element vanish when X enters (mute A/B), solo the clashing pair, sum to mono (stereo placement hides overlap), watch spectral peak overlap.
rationale: Stereo width creates the illusion of separation; the mono sum and enter/exit tests expose the true frequency conflict before any EQ move.
safety_notes: Дополняет lead_masking детектор (persistence 3 цикла, min_culprit_contribution 0.35); аранжировка решает ~99% места — вне власти пульта.

summary: Room/PA EQ is conservative: cuts of 2-3 dB first, low-end boosts spread across 63/80/100 Hz rather than one band; over-EQing is the classic mistake.
rationale: Room EQ fixes identified problems, it does not reshape the mix; aggressive graphic moves (+/-15 dB range available) destroy the system's tonality.
safety_notes: Совпадает с pa_v3 prefer-cut и гигиеническими кэпами.

summary: A small dip around 3 kHz in the house curve keeps loud levels painless (ear sensitivity peak); combines with a pink/tilted target, never a flat curve at show volume.
rationale: The ear's max sensitivity sits near 3 kHz; at concert SPL a flat response reads harsh. The dip softens without dulling.
safety_notes: Не дублировать дип, если мастер-EQ уже несёт срез в этой зоне (mirror/pink-balance).

summary: Room modes, corner bass buildup and the real house curve exist only in the ACOUSTIC domain: a measurement mic in the room is mandatory; the electric chain is blind to them.
rationale: The console's taps end at the PA input; reflections, modes and buildup happen in the air. Data-driven room decisions need a flat mic + analyzer (pink noise / transfer function).
safety_notes: Наш известный пробел: вся оценка сейчас электрическая; микрофон зала — в идеальной карте тапов (сервисная пара 45-46).

summary: WING: compressor and gate sidechains are full nodes /ch/N/dynsc|gatesc/{type,f,q,src,tap} with CROSS-CHANNEL src (SELF|CH.1..CH.40) and filter types OFF/LP12/HP12/BP/NOTCH.
rationale: Enables kick->bass ducking (bass dyn mdl DUCK + dynsc/src=kick) and vocal->guitars dynamic yielding without external processing; sidechain EQ unavailable when CMB model occupies the dyn slot.
safety_notes: Из документации, на пульте НЕ проверено: у WING бывают тихие отказы записи — обязательна readback-верификация src/tap токенов перед автоматизацией.

summary: WING: both GATE and DYN slots accept the full model list incl. DS902 (DBX 902 de-esser), DEQ/DEQ2 (dynamic EQ), DUCK, RIDE — a de-esser can live in the GATE slot while COMP keeps the dyn slot.
rationale: Solves the one-dyn-slot constraint for the canonical vocal chain: comp in dyn slot, DS902 in gate slot; DEQ2 covers dynamic-EQ masking fixes.
safety_notes: Параметрические токены моделей существуют только при загруженной модели (как у FX): читать после загрузки, ждать ~0.6 с; live-верификация обязательна.
Вокал теряет обычный гейт при DS902 в гейт-слоте — для вокала приемлемо (гейт на вокале и так не используется).

summary: WING: /ch/N/proc selects any of 24 Gate/EQ/Dyn/Insert orders (e.g. EDGI = subtractive EQ -> comp -> de-esser-in-gate-slot); /ch/N/peq is a SECOND EQ block (PreSend EQ).
rationale: The canonical vocal chain order (cuts pre-comp, de-ess post-comp) maps to WING natively via proc permutation; PEQ may host additive boosts post-dyn if its chain position allows (to verify on console).
safety_notes: Смена proc на живом канале может дать слышимый скачок — только в саундчек-фазе с журналом и откатом.

summary: Line check order: kick (solid solo hits) -> snare -> kick+snare alternating -> toms -> overheads -> bass -> guitars -> keys -> vocals; per-channel gain/gate/EQ/comp are set here, one source at a time.
rationale: The rhythm-section foundation is dialed first; solo solid hits (not patterns) give clean material for gain, gate thresholds and phase measurements without bleed ambiguity.

summary: Solo passes ARE the measurement material: isolated kick/snare hits feed phase alignment (GCC MAD gates), gate thresholds, OH ILD panning; the engine's deferred checklist items translate into requests to the band.
rationale: Waiting for isolated hits inside dense full-band material can take forever (run 21: 12 min, zero usable hits); asking the drummer for 5-10 solo snare hits closes the same items in 30 seconds.

parameters.example: drum_image.snare_to_oh deferred -> 'прошу 5-10 одиночных ударов по снейру без кика'

safety_notes: Фичу движка (список просьб из чек-листа) реализовать отдельной задачей.

summary: Two phases: line check (per-instrument processing) then full-band soundcheck (balance, masking, FX, monitor interaction); expect re-tweaks when the audience changes the acoustics.
rationale: Individual processing decisions need clean sources; balance and masking decisions only exist when everyone plays; the room changes when bodies absorb reflections.
safety_notes: Совпадает с архитектурой стадий движка (поканальные коррекции -> full-band shared-mix/balance/DCA).

summary: The mix target curve is genre-dependent: electronic is bass-dominant (sub+bass carry most energy), rock/pop keep stronger mids, acoustic runs lighter low end; applying one curve to every genre is a classic mistake.
rationale: A target curve is the skeleton of tonal balance, not a universal law; the master-loop deviation metric only means something against the right genre skeleton.
safety_notes: Наш master_mix.target_curve конфигурируем (сейчас pink по директиве оператора); смена кривой — операторское решение.

summary: Golden rule: compare the mix against a genre reference track through the SAME meter/curve; factory curves guide, they are not prescriptions.
rationale: Ears drift and rooms lie; a reference through identical measurement anchors decisions. Engine analogue: capture a reference's spectral curve and diff the master loop against it.

parameters.note: по умолчанию reference matching выключен (CLAUDE.md) — только явный запрос оператора

safety_notes: Reference matching в offline-пайплайне — только по явному запросу оператора (CLAUDE.md).

summary: Backing vocals sit BEHIND the lead: HPF up to ~300 Hz (body 150-250 reserved for the lead), LPF ~5-6 kHz (dark top reads as farther), less presence/air than the lead.
rationale: Depth perception: brighter = closer; reserving the lead's body and sharpness ranges keeps the chorus wide but the story in front.
safety_notes: Согласуется с Ayaic-плоскостью tucked backs (-27 LUFS) и приоритетом лид-вокала в маскинге.

summary: Backing vocals glue on a GROUP bus: bus compression 5-10 dB GR medium attack/release, bus de-essing, one shared (longer) reverb; pan symmetrically — tight harmonies ~10% off-center, unique lines hard L/R mirrored.
rationale: Bus processing fuses stacked voices into one chord instead of separate singers; symmetric panning keeps the image balanced while each part gets a pocket.
safety_notes: В текущем составе бэков нет; при появлении — группа-шина по образцу стем-шин, L/R пары под стерео-идентичность.

summary: Live drums prefer expander behaviour over a hard gate: downward ratios 2:1-4:1 with range/floor -10..-20 dB, never full mute — sudden silence draws attention.
rationale: An expander shapes bleed naturally; a slammed gate chops decays and reads as edits. Keeping some floor smooths transitions.
safety_notes: Подтверждает наш range -20 на барабанных гейтах; WING имеет EXP-модель в gate/dyn слотах.

summary: Gate chatter (rapid open/close around threshold) is fixed by hysteresis (second threshold), longer hold/release; attack is raised gradually until the opening click disappears.
rationale: Signals hovering at threshold flutter the gate; hysteresis separates open and close points. Too-fast attack clicks on transients.
safety_notes: CLAUDE.md: объявленный hysteresis ОБЯЗАН применяться в GateProcessor — подтверждено источником.

summary: Band-limit the gate key to the drum's trigger band (roll off irrelevant frequencies); the more low-frequency energy passes the key filter, the longer the gate stays open.
rationale: Unfiltered keys false-trigger on bleed; LF energy in the key stretches gate-open time — filter choice IS the gate timing.
safety_notes: Подтверждает sidechain HPF200/LPF4k барабанных гейтов; WING gatesc/{type,f,q} — та же поверхность.

summary: WING BDX902 de-esser: singing ~4.4 kHz / speech ~3 kHz frequency split, range NORMAL..6 dB (never deeper — muffling), HF ONLY on; detection is threshold-free (HF vs full-band ratio) and self-tracks varying live levels.
rationale: Relative detection needs no threshold rides as the vocalist works the mic; the frequency knob splits detection bands, range sets reduction depth.
safety_notes: Размещение: гейт-слот при COMP в dyn, порядок proc=EDGI (де-эсс после компрессора, правило vocal_chain.deess_after_comp); верифицировать mdl-загрузку readback'ом (тихие отказы).

summary: Sibilance bands by voice: male ~3-6 kHz (center 5-6k), female ~6-8 kHz (center 7-8k); set the de-esser split under the singer's band, verify by ear that only esses duck.
rationale: A de-esser tuned to the wrong octave either misses esses or chews consonants; the band is a property of the specific voice.
safety_notes: Наш sibilance_excess детектор уже следит за полосой — может выбирать частоту автоматически по спектру певца.

summary: Drum bus glue: ratio 2:1 (up to 4:1 for energy), attack 3-10 ms (10 preserves kick/snare punch), auto release, GR target 1-2 dB average; threshold is set LAST; restore lost level manually for honest A/B.
rationale: Bus compression is cohesion, not control: light GR with transient-preserving attack fuses the kit; deep bus GR flattens the mix's engine.
safety_notes: Шина DRUMS (bus 1) существует; BusCompressorAdjust не промоутнут — проба только по команде оператора; makeup под true-peak потолком.

summary: Parallel drum compression: a separate crushed path (max ratio, near-instant attack, GR 5-7+ dB) blended under the dry kit until barely audible; transients live in the dry signal.
rationale: Thickness without transient loss: the dry path keeps punch while the crushed path fills sustain between hits.

parameters.wing_plan: second bus fed by POST sends from drum channels, crushed comp, blended into main

safety_notes: Требует свободной шины и POST-посылов (GRP-посылы каналов фиксированы) — SETUP-раннер по команде оператора.

summary: Show time: the lead vocal is the money channel — ridden constantly; live spill forbids deep compression as a leveler, so level control is fader rides (or an auto-rider), and the vocal fader stays reachable on every layer.
rationale: Drum spill in the vocal mic turns heavy GR into a bleed pump; professionals ride instead and keep the vocal under a finger at all times.
safety_notes: WING RIDE (Waves Vocal Rider) — кандидат на пробу в dyn-слоте вокала; live-микрошаги фейдера уже ограничены lead_fader_max_step 0.5 дБ.

summary: Section dynamics at show time: pull the whole PA down 3-6 dB through verses, hit the chorus downbeat at unity — the crowd leans in, the chorus lands huge.
rationale: Perceived hugeness is contrast, not absolute level; the master matrix ride creates dynamics a static mix cannot.
safety_notes: MasterFaderMove у нас proposal-only и вниз-только — секционные райды остаются рукам оператора; автоматизация потребует явного промоута и детекции секций.

summary: Snapshots: one per song at most, recalled between songs; no mid-song snapshot chains; automatic recall is forbidden — recall overwrites the whole console state.
rationale: Pros stop short of intra-song snapshots: a recall mid-performance risks wiping live adjustments; recall is a deliberate operator act.
safety_notes: Совпадает с CLAUDE.md snap safety: find_snap_by_name читает только кэш имён; загрузка снапшота = деструкция состояния на концерте.
